from: UniProtKB release 2026_04: the reference proteome UP000006548 of Arabidopsis thaliana, 39,144 entries (16,217 reviewed, 22,927 unreviewed) for 27,368 genes. One protein is shown for each gene, the one that UniProt's own gene-by-gene set of the proteome gives: 27,368 proteins, 16,212 with a reviewed entry and 11,156 with an unreviewed one. The proteome's other 11,776 entries are further forms of the same genes; each protein counts its gene's entries in the mark 'entries'.

curated.note: A reviewed entry was written by a curator; an unreviewed one was annotated automatically, by rule systems and prediction programs. The table says, for the proteins shown, what stands behind each one's place.
rows: predicted from a segment or a signal

shelves.label: Cell membrane
shelves.outside: Outside the cell: in its wall and in the space around it
shelves.inside: Inside the cell: in the cytoplasm
shelves.note: A plant cell has a wall beyond its membrane. A protein of the wall, or of the space outside the membrane, stands here on the outside, and its mark 'where' names the wall. A protein of the plasmodesmata, the channels that join a plant's cells through the wall, stands on this shelf too.

shelves.label: Endoplasmic reticulum membrane
shelves.outside: On the cytoplasmic face of the endoplasmic reticulum

shelves.label: Plastid envelope
shelves.outside: On the cytoplasmic face of the plastid's envelope
shelves.inside: Within the plastid: in its stroma
shelves.note: The plastid's two envelope membranes stand as one shelf: a protein in either of them is in the envelope, and its mark 'where' says which where the entry does. A protein free in the stroma stands here, on the inside. Most of the plant's plastids are chloroplasts; the entries' words say which kind.

shelves.label: Thylakoid membrane
shelves.outside: In the plastid's stroma, at the thylakoid membrane
shelves.note: The membrane inside the chloroplast. Its lumen is on the inside; the stroma lies beyond it, so a protein held at this membrane and facing the stroma stands on the outside, while a protein free in the stroma stands on the plastid envelope's shelf.

shelves.label: Vacuole membrane
shelves.outside: On the cytoplasmic face of the vacuole's membrane
shelves.note: The membrane of the vacuole, a plant cell's largest compartment.

shelves.label: Nuclear envelope
shelves.outside: On the cytoplasmic face of the nuclear envelope

shelves.label: Other membranes
shelves.outside: On the cytoplasmic face of one of the other membranes
shelves.inside: Within one of the other compartments
shelves.note: The cell's remaining membranes together: those of the Golgi apparatus, endosomes, lysosomes, peroxisomes and vesicles, and the mitochondrion's outer membrane. Each protein here names its compartment in the mark 'where'.

shelves.label: A membrane, not told which
shelves.outside: Beyond a membrane: outside the cell, or within a compartment
shelves.inside: On the cytoplasmic side of a membrane
shelves.note: The proteins that an entry places in a membrane without naming it, and those with no stated place whose entry carries a membrane-spanning segment or a signal peptide.

plant.rule: The plastid has two levels. Its envelope, two membranes standing as one shelf, has the stroma inside it and the cytoplasm beyond: a protein in either membrane is in the envelope, and a protein free in the stroma stands on that shelf, inside. The thylakoid membrane lies in the stroma, with its lumen inside and the stroma beyond: a protein held at it and facing the stroma stands on the thylakoid's shelf, outside. The vacuole has a shelf of its own. A protein of the wall or of the space outside the cell membrane stands on the cell membrane's shelf, outside, as a secreted protein does, and so does one of the plasmodesmata, which join a plant's cells.

groups.label: Not classed by function

groups_from: A protein's Gene Ontology terms are those InterPro maps to any of its signatures and those UniProt gives its entry. With every broader term (by the ontology's kind-of and part-of links), the protein falls in the first district, in the order listed, one of whose terms it carries. A family's line stands in the district most of its classed members on that shelf fall in; of equal counts, the first listed. A protein that is the only member of its family stands in its own district. A part of no_family stands in a district only if more than half of all its members on that shelf fall there. The choice of the districts' terms and their order is the viewer's, and is the same for every species; the terms were chosen for animal cells, and a plant's own work (photosynthesis, the wall) falls under the districts they name.
family_from: A family is an InterPro entry of the type Family (InterPro 111.0). A protein is filed under the narrowest family among the InterPro entries UniProt gives it: one that is not a broader kind of another it carries, by InterPro's tree of entries. Where several unrelated families remain (1,098 proteins), it is the deepest in that tree, then the one fewest proteins of this catalogue are in, then the first by accession. This is the rule of every species' file, so a family has the same id in each.

family_notes.lines: A family has one line for each shelf that holds members of it, and one with a null shelf for its members that are on no shelf. A line is identified by id and shelf together; side, group, count, sides, file, at and units are of its members on that shelf alone.
family_notes.side: The side most of the line's members sit on; of equal counts, a membrane first.
family_notes.units: The inventory units with which the species' atlas lists a member on this line: as a candidate for the machine, where the member was found by the signature of a family that makes it, or as a part that goes with the machine, where 'found_by' names the member or the line.
family_notes.total: The family's members on every shelf and on none.
family_notes.counts: distinct_families is the number of families that have lines; families_in_all counts also the families of one, whose proteins are under 'lone'.

no_family.label: No family assigned
no_family.parts_from: A protein with no family is filed under one part. If it carries an InterPro entry of the type Homologous superfamily, the part is that superfamily: a wider grouping than a family, by shared structure. Of several superfamilies it is the one fewest proteins of this catalogue carry, then the first by accession. The other two parts hold the proteins with only a domain, repeat or site signature, and those with no signature at all. A part has one line for each shelf, as a family has.

members_from.order: The table's lines are the members in order: every line of the families as listed here, then every part of 'lone', then every part of 'no_family'; within each, by gene name. A line's members are the next 'count' lines of the table. For a family's line and for a part of no_family, 'under' is its id and 'shelf' its shelf (empty for none); for a part of 'lone', 'under' is the protein's own family and 'family' that family's name.
members_from.files: A file holds the members of consecutive lines: a new file begins where the next line would take it past 2,000 members, so a line is never split. 'file' names the file and 'at' the first and one past the last of its members there.
members_from.places: In the table a stated place is written with UniProt's identifiers, without their prefix: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them, joined by a full stop. 'place_words' gives the words of each.
members_from.step: python3 tools/build_thalecress_atlas.py members --out DIR writes the files from the two files.

side_notes.stated: The protein's UniProtKB entry states where it is, and the first place it states decides the shelf and the side. For a reviewed entry the statement is a curator's, and the mark 'evidence' says what stands behind it: an experiment, likeness to another protein, the curator's inference, or a rule. For an unreviewed entry no curator wrote it: the statement was made by one of UniProt's rule systems, and its evidence is 'rule'.
side_notes.predicted: Read from the entry's own features, where its words do not give the side. A membrane-spanning segment puts the protein in a membrane; a signal peptide with no such segment puts it on the side away from the cytoplasm. Where the entry states no place, the protein stands on the shelf of a membrane that is not named. A transit peptide, which sends a protein into a plastid or a mitochondrion, is not read here: where a curator states such a place on it, the place is stated. In a reviewed entry UniProt's pages name the predictors behind the predicted features: TMHMM, Memsat, Phobius and a hydrophobic moment plot for the segments; Phobius, Predotar, SignalP and TargetP for the signal peptides. In an unreviewed entry the program is named on each feature. Each is named among the sources, with its terms and what rests on it. By the project's rule (the user, 15 November 2026), a value stands on the terms of the database it was read from, and the tool behind it is named and counted: the project's rule, not a legal opinion.
side_notes.none: The entry states a membrane or a place and not the side (the protein then stands apart beside that shelf, with the place in its mark 'where'), or it states no place of the cell and carries no membrane-spanning segment and no signal peptide (the protein is then on no shelf). Nothing is placed by guess.

placed_by.what: The place itself is on one side: within a compartment, or beyond a membrane.
The entry states that the protein spans the membrane (single-pass or multi-pass).
The entry states which face of the membrane the protein is on.
The entry states a GPI anchor and no face: such an anchor holds a protein on the face away from the cytoplasm.
The first place names no side, and a later statement of the same entry names a part of that place and gives the side.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment and not the side, and it carries a membrane-spanning segment: in the membrane.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment and not the side, and it carries a signal peptide and no membrane-spanning segment: on the side away from the cytoplasm.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a membrane-spanning segment: in a membrane, not told which.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a signal peptide and no segment: beyond a membrane, outside the cell or within a compartment.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment, and nothing in it settles the side.
No place of the cell is stated and nothing is predicted: on no shelf.

place_kinds.membrane: the shelf's membrane, or a part of it
place_kinds.whole: a compartment that one membrane bounds, or a structure at the membrane, with no part or face named
place_kinds.region: a region with more than one membrane, or none
place_kinds.elsewhere: not a place of the cell

place_notes: Every place the entries state, in UniProt's words, with the shelf and what the place names against its membrane (place_kinds), how the table's line was reached and which of the table's terms it rests on, and how many proteins it places as the statement that decided.

found_by.note: How the species' atlas found each protein that it lists with a unit (schema/SPECIES_ATLAS.md, found_by). A protein with a unit is found by the signature of a family that makes the machine unless it is named under 'proteins'; one found only by the signature of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, or a subunit that makes none by itself) is listed with the unit and is no candidate for its own work, and the page draws it plain. A family is named under 'families' where every protein of it that has a unit was found so.

reviewed.label: Curated entry
reviewed.note: Whether the protein's UniProtKB entry is reviewed, written by a curator, or unreviewed, annotated automatically.

entries.label: Entries for its gene
entries.note: The proteome's entries for the same gene, by the Araport gene that UniProt gives each entry: this protein's own and the further forms of the gene. The marker stands for the one UniProt's gene-by-gene set names.

isoforms.label: Isoforms described
isoforms.note: The canonical sequence and the other sequences its own entry describes.

seen.label: Evidence that the protein exists
seen.note: UniProt's level of evidence for the entry: at protein level, at transcript level, inferred from homology, predicted, or uncertain.

evidence.label: What stands behind the stated place
evidence.note: From UniProt's evidence codes on the statement: an experiment in a paper the entry cites; likeness to a protein of which it is known; a curator's inference; a rule (a family rule or a sequence model that a curator applied, or, in an unreviewed entry, one of UniProt's automatic rule systems); not given, an older curated statement. Of several, the first in this order.

where.label: Stated place
where.note: The statement that decided the shelf, in UniProt's words: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them.

also.label: Also stated
also.note: The entry's other statements of place, in order and in UniProt's words.

family.label: Family, of which it is the only member here
family.note: The InterPro family's accession and name, for a protein listed among the only members of their families.

of.label: Stated for
of.note: The named form of the protein that the place is stated for, where the entry states none for the protein as a whole.
